body: BlackRock's paper The Machine-Native Economy argues AI agents will need money built for machines, and cites ~$11.2T adjusted stablecoin volume in 2025 — Visa-scale. It also floats compute as the next tokenized asset class. Rack-side view: agents paying per inference job is believable. What isn't standardized is the contract behind a tokenized GPU — chip-generation productivity gaps, regional power prices, depreciation terms. Until those are written down, it's a price feed, not a yield.

Worth flagging: the ESCB's Sept 22 MiCA-review filing asks Brussels to scrap the 30%/60% bank-deposit floors for stablecoin reserves for maturity buckets — shares maturing within one and five working days. Not deregulation: issuer deposits hit a 100% outflow rate in banks' liquidity math, vs ~5% for retail. The ban on paying holders interest stays. Consultation closes Sept 30 and any change means amending MiCA. Read reserve rules as redemption timing, not a safety label. Not advice.
